blocks.text: Original document: [docs/FONT_SYSTEM_ARCHITECTURE.md](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/docs/FONT_SYSTEM_ARCHITECTURE.md). See [current limitations](/limitations) for concrete compatibility notes.

Retiam is a high-performance WebGPU animation engine engineered for mathematical visualizations, cinematic educational motion graphics (in the style of 3Blue1Brown/Manim), and scientific simulations. Typography in Retiam serves two foundational rendering pipelines, each designed for distinct aesthetic and technical use cases:

children: Used by [`Text`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/composites/text/Text.ts), [`Code`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/composites/text/Code.ts), and analytical path-effect materials (`PathEffect`, `Chalk`, `Outline`).
Outlines are extracted as mathematical Bézier polynomial curves directly from TrueType/OpenType tables via `opentype.js`.

Renders with zero rasterization artifacts at infinite magnification and enables stroke-drawing animations (e.g., drawing chalk outlines glyph-by-glyph via [`Write`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/animation/Write.ts)).

Used by [`SDFText`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/composites/text/SDFText.ts) and closed-caption subtitles for high-throughput GPU-accelerated raster text at arbitrary scale, rotation, and 3D camera perspectives.
Unlike standard monochrome SDFs which round off sharp corners, MSDF packs three independent distance fields into RGB color channels, preserving crisp geometric corners and sub-pixel anti-aliasing.

blocks.text: Previously, MSDF atlas generation relied on an external Node.js WebSocket daemon (`server/msdf-server.ts` on `ws://localhost:5002`) running `msdf-bmfont-xml`. This introduced severe drawbacks:

items: **External Dependency**: Required developers to launch and maintain a secondary background terminal process (`npm run msdf-server`).
**Production Portability**: Failed completely in client-side web embeddings, documentation sites, and browser sandboxes where local Node.js processes cannot execute.
**Latency & Sockets**: WebSocket serialization overhead and socket reconnect flakiness introduced non-deterministic startup delays.

blocks.text: The modern Retiam font architecture is **100% autonomous, client-side, and in-browser**:

items: Generates MSDF distance fields inside a **dedicated Web Worker running WebAssembly (`msdfgen_wasm.wasm`)**.
Resolves **Google Fonts, custom remote URLs, and local files** entirely client-side.
Automatically handles **browser WOFF2 Brotli decompression** in WebAssembly.
Employs a **two-tier caching architecture** (Memory + persistent IndexedDB disk cache) with sub-2ms reloads.
Incorporates a mathematical **glyph inversion sanitizer** to correct backward contour windings in decorative, sketch, and grunge fonts.
Guarantees **bit-exact WebGPU texture ingestion** by preventing gamma warping and premultiplied alpha distortion.

blocks.content: All built-in aliases resolve through `FontResolver.ensureSfnt()` for transparent WOFF2/WOFF decompression, so bundled WOFF2 assets are always correctly decoded to TTF SFNT before being passed to `opentype.js` or `msdfgen`.

blocks.text: When querying `https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=...`, Google Fonts partitions font glyphs into unicode subsets (`cyrillic-ext`, `greek`, `vietnamese`, `latin`, etc.) using individual `@font-face` blocks.
If an engine naively selects the first `@font-face` block in the CSS response, it may load a subset containing Cyrillic or Greek glyphs while omitting standard Latin ASCII characters.
`FontResolver` inspects the CSS response and isolates the `/* latin */` section before extracting the binary font URL:
3.3 The Browser WOFF2 & WOFF 1.0 Challenge & WASM Solution
When a browser makes an HTTP request to Google Fonts, Google evaluates the browser's `User-Agent`:

items: **Chrome** receives WOFF2 (`.woff2`, compressed with Brotli, `wOF2` magic signature `0x774f4632`).
**Microsoft Edge, Safari, and Firefox** receive WOFF 1.0 (`.woff`, compressed with Deflate, `wOFF` magic signature `0x774f4646`).

Both native FreeType (used in `msdfgen_wasm.wasm`) and other low-level engines strictly expect uncompressed SFNT tables (TrueType `0x00010000` or OpenType `0x4f54544f`) and reject raw WOFF / WOFF2 with:

blocks.code: Error: Failed to load font from memory

items: Overriding the `User-Agent` header in browser `fetch()` is prohibited by the W3C Fetch specification.

blocks.text: **The Solution:** `FontResolver.ensureSfnt(buf)` inspects the first 4 bytes of any downloaded font stream:

items: If `wOF2` is detected, it dynamically loads `woff2-encoder/decompress` (WebAssembly Brotli decoder) to decompress to SFNT.
If `wOFF` is detected, it dynamically loads `opentype.js` to inflate the WOFF tables and serialize back into an SFNT buffer.

blocks.text: MSDF generation is computationally intensive. To keep 60 FPS animation playback fluid and prevent UI freezing, generation is offloaded to a dedicated Web Worker managed by `@zappar/msdf-generator` using Comlink RPC.
Vite URL imports are used to bundle the worker script and WASM binary:

import workerUrl from '@zappar/msdf-generator/worker.js?worker&url';
import wasmUrl from '@zappar/msdf-generator/msdfgen_wasm.wasm?url';

blocks.text: 5. Mathematical Root Causes & The Inversion Sanitizer
5.1 The Glyph Inversion Problem in Decorative & Sketch Fonts

When testing complex fonts such as *Fredericka the Great*, *Rubik Dirt*, or grunge fonts, certain characters (e.g. `'S'`, `'p'`, `'a'`, `'R'`) rendered as solid colored bounding boxes with the letter carved out of the middle, while simple fonts rendered normally.

`msdfgen` computes signed distance by raymarching glyph outline curves using FreeType. To determine whether a sample point $\mathbf{p} = (x, y)$ is **inside** or **outside** the glyph shape, `msdfgen` calculates the **winding number** $W(\mathbf{p})$ with respect to the closed boundary curves $\partial \Omega$:

items: **Outer boundaries** must have a clockwise (or counter-clockwise depending on the coordinate system) winding direction.
**Inner holes** (like the counter of an `'O'`) must have the opposite winding direction.

blocks.text: In sketch and decorative fonts, glyphs are constructed with thousands of overlapping pencil hatch lines. In several glyphs, the outermost perimeter stroke has a **reversed contour winding direction**.
Consequently, when `msdfgen` evaluates sample points in the empty padding around the letter:

The distance field assigns positive distance ($d = 255$) to the empty exterior, while assigning negative distance to the interior strokes. When the WebGPU shader evaluates `smoothstep(-edgeWidth, edgeWidth, sigDist)`, it treats the empty background as solid ink.
Every glyph in an MSDF atlas is rendered with safety padding (default: 2 to 4 pixels) around its bounding box to ensure distance field gradients do not clip at quad boundaries.
Therefore, **by geometric definition, the four corner pixels of any glyph quad must always reside in empty exterior space ($\text{median} \le 127$)**.
`MSDFGenerator.sanitizeInvertedGlyphs` inspects the four corners of every glyph quad in the atlas:

items: Corner pixels:
Evaluates the median distance value for each corner:

blocks.tex: M(R, G, B) = \max(\min(R, G), \min(\max(R, G), B))

items: If $\ge 3$ corners evaluate as inside ($M > 127$), the distance field for that glyph is inverted:

blocks.text: **Why $255 - d$ preserves the boundary:** In an 8-bit MSDF atlas, the exact glyph boundary is defined at $0.5$ (value 128). Because:
Inverting across 255 preserves the anti-aliased edge position within $< 0.4\%$ error while restoring the background to pure $0$ (transparent exterior).
Execution time for the entire 2048×2048 atlas is **$< 1\text{ms}$**.
6. Resolution, Nyquist Sampling & Bit-Exact Texture Ingestion
6.1 The Nyquist Sampling Limit for Sketch Fonts
When testing *Fredericka the Great*, initial renders appeared "melted" or low-resolution:

items: At default `fontSize: 48`, the glyph height is 48 texels.
Sketch fonts contain multiple overlapping pencil strokes whose width is $< 0.5\%$ of the font height ($< 0.24\text{px}$).

By the **Nyquist-Shannon sampling theorem**, resolving an edge transition requires at least 2 sample points across the feature width. When stroke spacing falls below 1 pixel in the atlas, distance gradients merge, turning fine pencil lines into rounded blobs.

blocks.text: **The Solution:** Retiam configures high-fidelity defaults for the MSDF pipeline:

items: `fontSize: 120` (up from 48 or 72)
`distanceRange: 10`
`textureSize: [2048, 2048]`

blocks.text: This provides **6.25× more sample area per glyph**, cleanly resolving ultra-fine sketch hatchings.
In Chromium browsers, `createImageBitmap()` defaults to applying color-space conversions and alpha premultiplication based on the host display profile:

Because MSDF textures encode **pure mathematical Euclidean distances** in the RGB channels rather than visual sRGB color information, any gamma transformation warps the linear distance slope, causing edge dilation, rounded corners, and anti-aliasing banding.

Retiam allows applying strokes to MSDF text via `paint.stroke` and `paint.stroke_width`. To guarantee that text stroke widths match vector primitives ([`Path`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/primitives/2d/Path.ts), [`Rect`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/primitives/2d/Rect.ts)) regardless of camera zoom or parent scale transforms:

The `FontStyle` type provides a zero-boilerplate way to use bundled fonts directly in any text entity via a plain string — no `FontLoader` call required. The engine resolves, decompresses, and caches the font automatically on first use.

blocks.content: `FontStyle` is accepted **only** by [`Text`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/composites/text/Text.ts) and [`SDFText`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/composites/text/SDFText.ts) via their `font` option. **`Tex`** uses a separate `fontStyle?: TexStyle` option — see §9.2.

blocks.text: `Tex` does **not** use `FontStyle`. Instead it accepts `fontStyle?: TexStyle` which selects a pre-patched MathJax SVG font variant:

blocks.code:
// src/engine/entities/composites/text/Tex.ts
export type TexStyle = 'default' | 'excalifont' | 'virgil';

blocks.content: Tex font patching works by injecting vector glyph dictionaries (defined in `TexFontPatcher.ts`) directly into MathJax's internal SVG font variant tables at document-creation time. Each style has its own isolated MathJax document cache to avoid prototype pollution between simultaneously active `Tex` entities.
